graft.title: rust profile: cargo-deny for advisories, bans and sources
graft.need: In profiles/rust: a scaffold deny.toml with [advisories], [bans] and [sources] only (licenses are Tend's, judged against the combo), exclude-dev and all-features in [graph], and a CI job that installs cargo-deny on the runner (taiki-e/install-action) and runs `cargo deny --workspace check advisories bans sources`. Not cargo-deny-action: it runs in a container whose musl toolchain a project's rust-toolchain.toml (the profile's own rule) overrides, and it fails.
graft.use_case: autodyne's deny.toml and CI job are exactly this today (deny.toml, ci.yml's deny job); every Rust project should get them from the profile instead of copying them.

answer.text: Recorded: the rust profile's scaffold now has deny.toml and .github/workflows/deny.yml, and its guidance says why cargo-deny runs on the runner. A Rust project gets both from `tend baseline render --write` where they're missing; autodyne already has its own.
